h1: The 8 Best Filing Cabinets for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Home Office Filing Cabinets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 filing cabinets for home offices compared on drawers, locks, mobility and footprint, from under-desk rollers to lateral units.
summary: The Letaya 3-drawer mobile cabinet is the best filing cabinet for most home offices: assembled, lockable and happy under a desk. The DEVAISE 2-drawer is the compact alternative, and the lateral Letaya suits rooms with wall space. Printer corners belong to the VASAGLE CUSTOS, while the SteeLoong is the plain metal fallback.
intro: Before you compare finishes or lock types, take a tape measure to the spot where the cabinet will live. A vertical drawer pulls out two feet or more toward you, a lateral one slides along the wall, and a rolling unit has to clear your knees. Plenty of buyers discover only after delivery that the top drawer collides with a chair.

Eight cabinets are ranked here across vertical, lateral and under-desk designs. Fit for a typical home office came first, followed by locks, mobility and whether the thing arrives assembled, since a steel cabinet is a slog to build. Everything comes from the listings, not from a loading test.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Fully assembled, locking, three drawers, rolls out from under a desk.
products.description:
Letaya's three-drawer mobile cabinet slides under a desk on its own wheels and arrives fully assembled. It takes letter, legal and A4 hanging files, includes a lock and sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Most rivals give up one of the three things a home office wants, which are no assembly, security and easy movement. The DEVAISE 2-drawer keeps all three but holds a drawer less, and the steel verticals lower down demand a screwdriver afternoon. That mix of convenience and capacity is what lifts the Letaya past the pack.

Choose it for a desk-side spot where you want tax records, IDs and everyday folders in one place. The caveat is clearance: three drawers need a fairly tall opening, so measure beneath your desk before ordering.
products.idealFor: Most home offices with a desk-side spot.
products.skipIf: You have no space under the desk.

products.name: DEVAISE 2 Drawer Metal File Cabinet, Fully Assembled, Under Desk, Black
products.verdict: Two locking drawers in a fully assembled metal under-desk cabinet.
products.description:
DEVAISE's two-drawer metal cabinet is a fully assembled under-desk unit in black with a lock, taking letter, legal and A4 files. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It matches the Letaya on convenience yet gives up a drawer, which is the reason it is second. In return it slips under desks the three-drawer model cannot clear and keeps a tidy profile. It is also the priciest cabinet in the ranking, so you pay extra for the compact package and the metal build.

Pick it if your desk has limited leg space or you only keep a modest folder collection. Skip it if you are a heavy filer, because two drawers fill quickly and the money is better spent on the Letaya.
products.skipIf: You file a lot of paper.

products.name: Letaya 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Metal Lateral Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A lateral metal cabinet that needs less front-to-back clearance.
products.description:
This Letaya lateral cabinet has two metal drawers that open sideways, measures 27.95 x 28.35 x 15.74 inches and includes a lock. It handles letter, legal and A4 files and costs $50 to $100.

Lateral designs earn their place in rooms where you cannot pull a deep drawer toward the middle of the floor, since the drawers slide along the wall instead. That flexibility lifts it above the DEVAISE rolling lateral, which lacks a stated lock. The trade is width: it wants a clear stretch of wall and will not tuck under a desk.

Buy it for a narrow spare room or hallway office with side space. Skip it if wall room is scarce, because the wide footprint is its one real drawback.

products.name: DEVAISE 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet, Lateral Filing Cabinet, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: Three lateral drawers on casters in a rustic brown finish.
products.description:
The DEVAISE rolling lateral cabinet packs three sideways drawers on casters in a rustic brown finish, and it takes letter, legal and A4 files. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Compared with the metal Letaya lateral above, you get an extra drawer, wheels and a warmer look that blends into living-space offices. What you lose is security, since the listing mentions no lock. That single omission keeps it fourth, because paperwork storage is mostly about keeping private documents private.

It suits a home office that doubles as a living area where appearance counts and the files are not sensitive. Anyone storing financial records should choose a locking cabinet higher on the list. It is also wide, so check wall space first.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS 2-Drawer File Cabinet, Small Rolling Filing Cabinet, Matte Black
products.verdict: A 15.7 x 16.5 x 27.6 inch rolling cabinet that doubles as a printer stand.
products.description:
VASAGLE's CUSTOS is a small two-drawer rolling cabinet in matte black, measuring 15.7 x 16.5 x 27.6 inches. It takes letter and A4 files, and its top is designed to hold a printer. It lands in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Its double duty is the appeal: one compact footprint covers both paper storage and the printer, and it rolls out of the way. It ranks fifth because the listing names no legal-size support and no lock, so it cannot hold the same range of documents as the models above.

Choose it for a printer corner in a small room, where blank paper and recent copies are the main contents. Skip it if you file legal-size documents or anything confidential. Check the printer weight against the stated top surface before you commit.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24 Inch Extended Desktop
products.verdict: A mobile two-drawer cabinet with a 24 inch extended desktop surface.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO is a mobile two-drawer unit with fabric drawer fronts, a 24 inch extended desktop surface and a side bag, rolling on casters. It fits letter and A4 files and falls in the $50 to $100 bucket.

The extra surface turns a storage box into a mini workstation, which is useful in a small workspace with little desk. It ranks sixth because fabric fronts cannot lock and feel less sturdy than the metal cabinets, so it falls behind the VASAGLE if you only need paper storage.

Buy it if you need a small work surface and low-stakes files. The caveat is security, since no lock is listed. Keep tax documents, passports and similar papers in a metal cabinet from higher up the ranking instead.
products.idealFor: A small workspace that needs a surface.

products.name: BYNSOE 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Vertical Steel Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A vertical steel cabinet with a lock that needs less side clearance.
products.description:
BYNSOE is a two-drawer vertical steel cabinet with a lock, built for letter-size files. Assembly is required, and it sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

The steel body and lock suit paperwork you want protected, and a vertical layout needs less side clearance than a lateral unit, so it fits a narrow wall in a spare room. What drops it to seventh is the combination of assembly time, a letter-only listing and no wheels, all of which the Letaya models avoid.

Pick it for a fixed home against a wall, with standard paperwork. Skip it if you want something pre-built or need legal or A4 support, since the listing mentions letter size only.
products.idealFor: A narrow wall in a spare room.

products.name: SteeLoong 2 Drawer File Cabinet, Metal Office File Cabinet with Lock, Black
products.verdict: A standard two-drawer metal cabinet with a lock and no extras.
products.description:
SteeLoong is a plain two-drawer metal cabinet in black with a lock and a standard office design. It also sits in the $50 to $100 bucket, matching most of the field on price.

There is little to criticize and little to praise. The listing gives few specs and no standout features, so it cannot beat models that add wheels, a desktop or file-size versatility. On the other hand, you pay for nothing you do not need, and a metal body with a lock covers the basics.

Buy it if you want an unremarkable cabinet that does the one job. Skip it if you want mobility, extra surface or listed file-size support. Before ordering, confirm the dimensions, since the listing offers little detail.

whatMatters.factor: Choose the shape for your room
whatMatters.detail: Vertical drawers pull toward you and need front room, lateral drawers slide sideways and need wall width, and rolling cabinets must fit beneath a desk. The wrong shape means drawers that will not fully open. Measure clearance in front, to the side and under the desk, then compare with the listing dimensions.

Letter is the US standard, legal runs longer and A4 is the international size. A cabinet that cannot hang your file size wastes the purchase. The Letaya and DEVAISE models list all three, while BYNSOE lists letter only. Read the bullets for supported sizes before choosing.

A lock keeps tax records, IDs and contracts private from visitors or kids. Metal cabinets such as the Letaya, DEVAISE 2-drawer and SteeLoong list one, while fabric fronts like the GYIIYUO cannot lock. Check the description for a lock or key mention, and confirm the lock is included.

Steel cabinets are heavy and fiddly to put together, so assembly can eat an afternoon. Fully assembled models, like the Letaya and DEVAISE 2-drawer, save that effort but arrive in bulkier boxes. Search the listing for the words fully assembled or assembly required before you buy.

Casters let you roll a cabinet out for access and away when you need legroom. They matter in small offices where space changes through the day. Look for rolling or mobile in the title, and check whether the casters can lock so the cabinet does not drift when you pull a drawer.

faq.q: What is the best filing cabinet for a small office?
faq.a: For a small office, the DEVAISE 2-drawer or Letaya 3-drawer work best, because they tuck beneath a desk and roll out for access. The Letaya holds more, while the DEVAISE has the slimmer profile.

For financial or personal documents, yes. The Letaya cabinets, the DEVAISE 2-drawer, BYNSOE and SteeLoong all list locks. The GYIIYUO has fabric fronts and no lock, so keep sensitive papers elsewhere.

faq.q: What is a lateral file cabinet?
faq.a: A lateral cabinet has wide drawers that slide sideways along the wall. It needs less front-to-back clearance than a vertical model, which is why the Letaya lateral suits narrow rooms, though it demands more width.
The Letaya and DEVAISE models list letter, legal and A4. The VASAGLE CUSTOS lists letter and A4 only, and the BYNSOE lists letter only, so check before filing legal documents in them.

faq.q: Can a filing cabinet double as a printer stand?
faq.a: Yes, the VASAGLE CUSTOS is designed for it, with a printer-stand top and a compact rolling body. Check the printer's weight against the listing before putting a heavy laser model on it.
The Letaya 3-drawer and DEVAISE 2-drawer list full assembly. The BYNSOE requires assembly, and the listing for the lateral models gives less detail, so confirm it on the product page.

finalTake: Start with your floor plan, then your paperwork. The Letaya 3-drawer fits most desk-side spots and locks, the DEVAISE covers tighter ones, and the lateral models solve front-clearance problems. If you handle sensitive documents, skip the fabric-fronted GYIIYUO. Everything else comes down to how much paper you really keep.
